body:
## Why

`trip_planner/app/main.py:62-73` deliberately keeps the API up when database initialisation fails ("Resilient startup … keep the API up so /api/health passes"), after a managed Postgres expired and every deploy was marked failed. That choice is sound and this issue does not reverse it.

The defect is what health then reports. `trip_planner/app/routes/health.py:11-17` returns `status: "ok"` unconditionally, so a service whose database never initialised says it is healthy. Observed 2026-09-22 during the audit: a backend started against a database stamped at a newer migration answered `/api/health` 200 `ok`, and the only way to learn it was degraded was to exercise a trip route. A gate that goes silent at exactly the moment it should report is the pattern this workspace calls a latched gate: the check cannot say what would clear it.

## Scope

`main.py` startup, `routes/health.py`, the `HealthStatus` schema, the `/health` page.

## Non-Goals

Do not make health return non-200 on a degraded database (that restores the crash-loop failure the resilient startup exists to prevent).

## Tasks

- [ ] Update `trip_planner/app/main.py` to record the database startup outcome on app state: ready or failed with the exception class.
- [ ] Update `trip_planner/app/routes/health.py` and the `HealthStatus` schema to return HTTP 200 with `status: "degraded"` and `database: {"ready": false, "reason": "<exception class>"}` after failed initialisation, and `status: "ok"` only after success.
- [ ] Update the `/health` page to show the degraded state in words.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Test gate `tests/app/test_health_degraded.py`: with `ensure_database_ready` patched to raise, `/api/health` returns 200 with `status == "degraded"` and `database.ready is False`; unpatched it returns `status == "ok"`. Deliberate break: hard-code `status="ok"` and the gate fails; reverting passes.

## Implementation Notes

_Not provided._
